ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Seventy percent (70%) of the injured employee's average weekly wage, not to exceed the state average weekly wage (85A O.S. § 45(A)(1)), as amended by HB2367 effective May 29, 2019.
ttd.minText: The Administrative Workers' Compensation Act sets no minimum weekly TTD rate, and the WCC maximum-rate chart lists none.
ttd.periodLabel: injuries from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026 (the SAWW takes effect January 1 of the year after its determination, 85A O.S. § 2(24))

waiting.text: There is no payment for the first three days of the initial period of temporary total disability (85A O.S. § 45(A)(1)); the Act provides no retroactive payment of these days.

ttdDuration.text: TTD is payable for up to 156 weeks; an administrative law judge may extend it by up to 52 more weeks for a consequential injury needing more time to reach maximum medical improvement, on clear and convincing medical evidence (85A O.S. § 45(A)(1)).

ppd.text: Permanent partial disability is 70% of the average weekly wage, capped at $375 per week for injuries on or after July 1, 2025 (WCC chart; $360 from July 1, 2021), for the proportion of 350 weeks that the disability bears (body as a whole up to 360 weeks), rated under the AMA Guides, Sixth Edition for non-scheduled parts (85A O.S. § 45(C)).

facts.text: Oklahoma pays 70% of the average weekly wage, not two-thirds, for temporary total, permanent partial and permanent total disability.

The employer may terminate TTD if the worker misses three consecutive medical appointments without valid excuse or abandons care; benefits end permanently after 60 days of noncompliance (85A O.S. § 45(A)(2)).
Temporary partial disability (70% of the wage difference for alternative work) is limited to 52 weeks, and refusing offered alternative work forfeits TTD and TPD (85A O.S. § 45(B)).
Before HB2367 (May 29, 2019) the TTD maximum was 70% of the state average weekly wage ($607.40 in early 2019); it is now 100% ($867.71 from May 28, 2019).
